content: The document provides detailed guidelines and standards for agricultural pesticide application equipment, including minimum requirements and related testing procedures. Additionally, it addresses the prevention of accumulation and proper disposal of obsolete pesticide stocks through an environmental management toolkit. The International Code of Conduct on Pesticide Management, collaboratively developed by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the World Health Organization (WHO), establishes a comprehensive framework and standards for managing pesticides throughout their lifecycle. This Code is widely recognized as a global reference for pesticide management and is primarily directed at government authorities and the pesticide industry, though it is also relevant to other stakeholders. First published in 1985 as the International Code of Conduct on the Distribution and Use of Pesticides, the Code has undergone several updates, with the current fourth version released jointly by FAO and WHO in 2014. This latest version places greater emphasis on public health pesticides, the health and environmental impacts of pesticides, and the protection of vulnerable groups. It also references relevant multinational environmental agreements, addresses the management of highly hazardous pesticides, and updates terms and definitions to align with advancements in industrial chemical management. The Code outlines specific articles covering various aspects of pesticide management, including: 1. Objectives of the Code 2. Terms and definitions 3. Pesticide management 4. Testing of pesticides 5. Reducing health and environmental risks 6. Regulatory and technical requirements 7. Availability and use of pesticides 8. Distribution and trade 9. Information exchange 10. Labeling, packaging, storage, and disposal 11. Advertising These articles collectively provide a structured approach to ensuring the safe, effective, and environmentally responsible use of pesticides.
